title: High block: jump on the back pass
titleKid: They pass back: go and chase
brief: You are pressing their #6, who has their back to goal.
briefKid: You are chasing their midfielder, who is facing away from our goal.
question: Their #6 has played it back to their centre-back. Where do you go?
questionKid: They passed it back to their defender. Where do you go?

takeaway.standard: A back pass is the signal for a high block: the striker jumps first and presses the centre-back, and the whole team pushes up behind you.
takeaway.kid: When they pass back, chase the defender with the ball. Your team follows you.

misconceptions.text: You stayed on their #6 after the ball had gone, so their centre-back has all the time in the world to pick a pass.
misconceptions.textKid: The ball went back. Run at the defender who has it now.

misconceptions.text: You came at them from the touchline side, which leaves them the easy pass inside; press from the inside and show them down the line.
misconceptions.textKid: Come at them from the middle side, so they can only pass down the line.

notes: answer.ideal keyed on the inside shoulder (81.5, 27) once press.js leaned inside for a carrier off the middle in their half (the curved run: D2, R5). Before that the engine pressed on the ball-to-goal line and graded the inside approach down, which contradicted the pressed-from-the-outside text. If the press rule stops leaning inside, rewrite that text to match what is graded.
